summary: Abe proves Serre's conjecture on the higher-dimensional Artin character in equal characteristic: for a regular local ring containing a finite field with an admissible finite group action, a_G is the character of a Qℓ-rational representation. The proof reduces, by Kato–Saito–Saito, to a trace identity for a Fourier nearby cycle (Theorem 1.6), obtained from Lu–Zheng's relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace after a universally locally acyclic extension over an alteration (Theorem 1.5), and compares that nearby cycle with Laumon's total-dimension representation (Proposition 2.5) to get Qℓ-rationality. 107 items (10 library, 8 planned, 89 missing) are routed to EDC.8 and LPV.0 and to four Part IIs (equivariant traces, relative traces, general-base Fourier, geometric Artin representations). Six findings are recorded, all in the arXiv v2 text as well: a fixed-scheme identification in the proof of Theorem 1.6 (E3), the coefficient scope of the Lu–Zheng citation (E4), and four slips in the concluding remarks (E1, E2, E5, E6).

items.name: Module length
items.statement: For a ring R and R-module M, Module.length R M is the extended natural composition length; use IsNoetherian and IsArtinian to establish finiteness before extracting a natural number. Over a division ring with M finite-dimensional it equals finrank.

uses.how: Higher-dimensional Artin class function
Fixed-length invariance under the henselian comparison

items.name: Character of a finite-dimensional representation
items.statement: For a representation ρ over a commutative coefficient ring and finite free underlying module, χρ(g)=trace(ρ(g)); over a field χρ(1)=finrank, and isomorphic representations have equal characters.

uses.how: Existing split representation ring
Actual realization versus coefficient rationality
Equivariant perfect trace

items.name: Existing split representation ring
items.statement: For a field L and group G, TauCeti.repRing L G is the split Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional representations and repRingCharacter its character map. This is not by itself K0 of a derived perfect category.

uses.how: Characteristic-zero finite-group character injectivity
Actual realization versus coefficient rationality
Regular-character ambiguity in a nonidentity trace identity
Perfect representation K0 equals the split representation ring

items.name: Characteristic-zero finite-group character injectivity
items.statement: For finite G and any characteristic-zero field L, repRingCharacter is injective. Actual objects of FDRep L G with the same character are isomorphic. No algebraic-closedness hypothesis is required by these pinned declarations.

items.name: Triangulated Grothendieck group
items.statement: For an essentially small pretriangulated category with the required additive shift structure, TriangulatedK0 is generated by objects modulo distinguished-triangle relations. It is an existing generic carrier; specifying the correct perfect/equivariant subcategory is additional work.

uses.how: Shift sign in triangulated K0
Perfect-complex and representation Grothendieck groups
Equivariant perfect trace
Additivity of the group-element trace
Bounded-complex Euler–Poincaré identity in abelian K0

items.name: Shift sign in triangulated K0
items.statement: Under the pinned triangulated-category hypotheses, the class of X[1] is −[X], and the general integer-shift formula is multiplication by (−1)^n. In particular a vector space concentrated in cohomological degree 1 has negative class.

items.name: Derived sheaf tensor and coefficient change
items.statement: On the small étale sites used here, construct derived tensor, internal Hom and coefficient change using K-flat/K-injective models; compare with the ordinary derived category and preserve the coherent composition data needed for correspondences.

uses.how: Constructible finite-Tor étale coefficient category
Cohomological correspondence Grothendieck construction
Continuity of derived Hom
Equivariant perfect trace
Regular Galois local-system descent
Equivariant nearby-cycle tensor interchange
Projection formula on the strict-local Milnor-fiber diagram

items.name: Constructible finite-Tor étale coefficient category
items.statement: For the finite-type/noetherian situations covered by EDC.0, form Dctf(X,Λ), its finite coefficient changes, and the duality/six-operation interfaces with their stated finiteness hypotheses. The coherent non-Noetherian base extension in A10–A18 is not included merely by this import.

uses.how: Ordinary cohomological correspondence and fixed-point trace
Trait nearby and vanishing cycles
Cohomological correspondence Grothendieck construction
Artin–Schreier Fourier kernel
Regular Galois local-system descent
Katz canonical-extension Swan model

items.name: Ordinary cohomological correspondence and fixed-point trace
items.statement: For a correspondence c=(c1,c2):Z→X×S X with a map c1*F→c2!F, construct its trace on the fixed scheme using duality, and proper-pushforward/restriction compatibility where the ordinary EDC.8 hypotheses hold. Numerical trace additionally needs the appropriate proper integration.

uses.how: Relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace
Trace of the constant sheaf is fixed intersection length
Trace of a point-supported complex

items.name: Trait nearby and vanishing cycles
items.statement: For the excellent finite-type henselian-trait coefficient setting of LPV.0, construct RΨ, continuous inertia, specialization and i*F→RΨ(j*F)→RΦ(F)→, with strict-local Milnor-fiber stalks, proper/smooth base change and finite coefficient change. General coherent-base goodness is a separate continuation.

uses.how: Good nearby cycles and cohomological properness
Étale spreading of the geometric action
Perfectness of the Fourier nearby stalk
The infinity fiber identifies with nearby cycles
Local Fourier transform from 0 to infinity
Katz–Laumon vanishing for the constant full-trait input
Localization converts the local identity to vanishing cycles
Milnor-fiber base change to the one-dimensional parameter
Smooth local fiber has constant pushforward
Vanishing cycles commute with the strict-local pushforward comparison

items.name: Stable lattices for continuous compact actions
items.statement: A finite-dimensional L-vector space, L finite over Qℓ, with continuous action of a profinite group admits a stable OL-lattice; apply this to Γ×G. The proof uses compactness, not a finite image assumption.

items.name: Numerical Artin and Swan conductors
items.statement: Use the ramification filtration to define numerical Artin/Swan conductors with finite-quotient independence and their stated induction formulas from R01.3. This does not supply projective integral Swan modules or the higher-dimensional local Artin character.

uses.how: Projective integral Swan module
Local Fourier rank formula
Local Fourier preservation of Swan conductor

items.name: Admissible regular-local group action
items.statement: Package exactly C1's regular local ring, finite action, finite invariant extension, isolated nonidentity fixed quotients and unchanged residue field. Positive characteristic and invertibility of ℓ are separate hypotheses for the theorem, not part of the bare action.

uses.how: Fixed ideal and scheme-theoretic fixed locus

items.name: Fixed ideal and scheme-theoretic fixed locus
items.statement: For an automorphism σ of A, Iσ is generated by a−σ(a); for an automorphism σ of X, X^σ is the equalizer of σ and id. For affine X it is Spec(A/Iσ). Retain its nilpotent structure.

uses.how: Higher-dimensional Artin class function
Étale spreading of the geometric action

items.name: Higher-dimensional Artin class function
items.statement: Under C1 define aG(σ)=−length_A(A/Iσ) for σ≠1 and aG(1)=−Σσ≠1 aG(σ). In the geometric setting use OX,x and the fixed subscheme stalk. This defines an integer-valued function before any representation is constructed.

uses.how: Conjugacy invariance of the local Artin function
Geometric Serre conjecture: positivity
Regular-character ambiguity in a nonidentity trace identity
Tame curve tower different formula
Trace of the constant sheaf is fixed intersection length

items.name: Conjugacy invariance of the local Artin function
items.statement: Under C1, τ transports Iσ to Iτστ⁻¹ and preserves the local quotient length; hence aG is conjugacy invariant.

items.name: Actual realization versus coefficient rationality
items.statement: For an integer class function a and a characteristic-zero field L, distinguish existence of an actual finite-dimensional Qbarℓ[G]-module with character a from existence of an L[G]-module realizing a after extension of scalars. Being L-valued or a virtual character is not by definition L-realizability.

uses.how: Geometric Serre conjecture: positivity

items.name: Geometric Serre conjecture: positivity
items.statement: Under C1 with A containing a finite field and ℓ invertible in A, aG is the character of an actual finite-dimensional Qbarℓ-representation of G.

items.name: Geometric Serre conjecture: Qℓ realization
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses as G06, the Artin representation is realizable over Qℓ for every ℓ invertible in A. This is stronger than a Qℓ-valued virtual trace identity.

items.name: Regular-character ambiguity in a nonidentity trace identity
items.statement: For a finite group G over a characteristic-zero field, adding a multiple of the regular character changes only the value at 1. Therefore the nonidentity trace formula alone does not fix the normalized identity value, positivity or rational descent.

items.name: Tame curve tower different formula
items.statement: For a tower of finite separable smooth curve germs X→qY→gS over an algebraically closed field, d(f)=d(q)+e(q)d(g), where d is the local different exponent and e the ramification index. For the quotient by G at a unique totally ramified point e(q)=|G| and d(q)=aG(1). Thus μf−aG(1)=e(q)d(g), not in general d(g).

items.name: Identity-element trace under an étale quotient parameter
items.statement: In the dimension-one specialization of C2, if f factors through q:X→X/G and g:X/G→S is étale at q(x), then d(g)=0 and μf=aG(1), so the formula of Theorem 1.6 also holds at σ=1. This is not an unconditional extension in higher dimension.

items.name: Dualizable objects in a symmetric monoidal 2-category
items.statement: For a symmetric monoidal 2-category C, a dual of X consists of X∨, evaluation X∨⊗X→1 and coevaluation 1→X⊗X∨ with invertible triangle 2-cells. End(C) uses dualizable X equipped with an endomorphism; ΩC is the category EndC(1), not merely a set.

uses.how: Categorical trace and its functoriality

items.name: Categorical trace and its functoriality
items.statement: For dualizable X and e:X→X, tr(e) is coev followed by e⊗id, the symmetry and ev, an object of ΩC. Lu–Zheng's adjointable morphisms of endomorphisms induce trace morphisms and make a trace functor. The latter coherence is an explicit supplier gate, not just an objectwise formula.

uses.how: Trace commutes with symmetric monoidal functors
Relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace

items.name: Trace commutes with symmetric monoidal functors
items.statement: A symmetric monoidal 2-functor F preserves duals and induces a coherent isomorphism F(trC(e))≅trD(F(e)), including pairing functoriality.

items.name: Correspondence 2-category
items.statement: For coherent S, Corr(S) has separated finite-type S-schemes as objects, spans X←Z→Y as 1-morphisms, and proper maps between span vertices compatible with their two legs as 2-morphisms. Composition is fiber product, tensor is product over S, unit is S. Product over S is not asserted to be the categorical product in Corr(S).

uses.how: Cohomological correspondence Grothendieck construction

items.name: Cohomological correspondence Grothendieck construction
items.statement: For the torsion coefficients and schemes in the Lu–Zheng setup, the right-lax symmetric monoidal pseudofunctor assigns D(X,Λ) to X and g_!f* to a span X←fZ→gY, with the reversed 2-cell convention. Its Grothendieck construction has objects (X,F) and arrows given by a span with f*F→g^!G (equivalently g_!f*F→G). Use distinct notation for g_! and g^!.

uses.how: Relative dual and fixed trace target

items.name: Relative dual and fixed trace target
items.statement: For X→S write KX/S=f^!ΛS and DX/S(F)=RHom(F,KX/S). For an endocorrespondence z:Z→X×S X put X^z=Z×X×S X X via the diagonal. A trace class lies in H⁰(X^z,KX^z/S).

uses.how: Local acyclicity characterizes dualizability
Relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace
Relative Verdier dual represents the categorical dual

items.name: Local acyclicity characterizes dualizability
items.statement: With S Noetherian, Λ Noetherian commutative torsion and its annihilating integer invertible on S, X separated finite type and F∈Dctf(X,Λ), (X,F) is dualizable in CS,Λ iff F is locally acyclic over S; its dual is (X,DX/S F). Universal local acyclicity implies the same statement without needing the extra LA⇒ULA input.

items.name: Relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace
items.statement: For a ULA coefficient object (X,F) and endocorrespondence (z,w), take its categorical trace to obtain τS(z,w)∈H⁰(X^z,KX^z/S). This extends the ordinary EDC.8 construction; it does not replace it with an unrelated carrier.

uses.how: Base change of relative trace
Relative trace is constant on the connected parameter cover

items.name: Base change of relative trace
items.statement: For g:T→S in the noetherian setup of C4 and a ULA (X,F), the base-change transformation on the fixed-locus dualizing cohomology sends τS(z,w) to τT(g*(z,w)); the construction follows from the symmetric monoidal pullback, not an arbitrary base-change isomorphism of all f^! complexes.

items.name: Continuity of derived Hom
items.statement: For a small filtered inverse system of coherent schemes Xi with affine transition maps and Noetherian Λ, pullback induces colimj HomD(Xj)(Fj,Gj)≅HomD(X∞)(F∞,G∞) for F∈Dc⁻(Xi,Λ), G∈D⁺(Xi,Λ). Reduce by bounded truncations and constructible j!Λ generators to étale cohomology continuity.

items.name: Continuity of bounded constructible derived categories
items.statement: Under A10's inverse-system and coefficient hypotheses, 2-colimi Dcb(Xi,Λ)→Dcb(X∞,Λ) is an equivalence. Essential surjectivity descends cohomology truncations and their connecting morphism, then takes the cone; it is not only descent of cohomology groups.

items.name: Good nearby cycles and cohomological properness
items.statement: For a finite-presentation f and the torsion coefficient context of Theorem 1.5, record f-goodness as compatibility of the oriented-topos nearby-cycle object with all base changes in the source's sense, and cohomological properness of the relevant strict-local maps. These are separate predicates and neither is ordinary properness of f.

uses.how: Alteration/modification for good constructible nearby cycles
Local acyclicity over an absolute integral closure
The infinity fiber identifies with nearby cycles
Milnor-fiber base change to the one-dimensional parameter

items.name: Alteration/modification for good constructible nearby cycles
items.statement: Under the exact finite coefficient, finite-presentation and coherent-base hypotheses needed in Theorem 1.5, import Orgogozo's alteration for goodness/cohomological properness and modification ensuring constructibility. Reconstruct the noetherian-approximation and general-base hypotheses from the original theorems before treating this as a closed interface.

items.name: Absolute-integral-closure extension from the generic fiber
items.statement: After reduction to integral S with geometric generic point ξ, let Sbar be its normalization in ξ and j:Xξ→XSbar. Define E=Rj*Fξ. Prove that it is constructible of finite Tor dimension by the modification, oriented-topos point equivalence, enough-points argument and descent along a surjective map of coherent schemes.

uses.how: Local acyclicity over an absolute integral closure

items.name: Local acyclicity over an absolute integral closure
items.statement: In A14 after the chosen cohomologically proper alteration, compare a strict-local stalk with its generization and then the geometric Milnor fiber. Absolute integral closedness identifies the relevant strict henselizations with localizations; cohomological properness supplies the second comparison. Descend local acyclicity through the integral surjection using lifted specializations, then use goodness to get ULA.

items.name: Finite-stage descent of extension and chosen endomorphism
items.statement: In Theorem 1.5 descend the alteration through finite S′→S, then descend the constructible complex, its isomorphism with F over U, and the given α successively using Lemma 1.4. ULA and finite Tor descend through the integral surjection via the Milnor-fiber comparison. This proves a chosen endomorphism extends; a coherent simultaneous action of every element of G is not a stated conclusion.

items.name: ULA extension after a surjective alteration
items.statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring with p invertible, S a coherent Fp-scheme with finitely many irreducible components, U⊂S open, f:X→S finitely presented, F∈Dctf(XU,Λ) ULA over U, σ an S-endomorphism and α:σU*F→F. There are a surjective alteration T→S, G∈Dctf(XT,Λ) ULA over T and β:σT*G→G restricting to (F,α) over T×S U. No properness assumption on f or automorphism hypothesis on σ is added.

items.name: Finite-cover refinement under generic goodness
items.statement: In A17, if Fη is f-good for every geometric generic point η of S in the cited sense, T→S may be chosen finite. This is a separately cited refinement, not a conclusion proved in Abe's Theorem 1.5 argument.

items.name: Artin–Schreier Fourier kernel
items.statement: For char(k)=p, ℓ≠p and a permitted coefficient ring containing a nontrivial ψ:Fp→Λ×, construct the rank-one Artin–Schreier sheaf Lψ from the finite étale torsor u↦u^p−u. Pull back along the product ft′, then extend by zero from the t′-affine/generic locus as specified in C2.

uses.how: Perfectness of the Fourier nearby stalk
Connected curve cover with an extended coefficient endomorphism
Local Fourier transform from 0 to infinity
Perfect regular Fourier complex over the group ring
Katz–Laumon vanishing for the constant full-trait input
Projection formula on the strict-local Milnor-fiber diagram
Fourier family relating Katz and Laumon models

items.name: Étale spreading of the geometric action
items.statement: In C2 spread X, f and the finite G-action to an étale neighborhood Si of A¹ at 0 by finite-presentation descent. Shrink until nonidentity fixed supports lie over the distinguished point and f is smooth elsewhere. Nearby cycles are unchanged under this strict-henselian comparison.

items.name: Fixed-length invariance under the henselian comparison
items.statement: In A20, the isolated fixed local algebra is Artinian with unchanged residue field, so its étale/strict-henselian base-change comparison preserves its length. Do not identify the entire fixed scheme with its closed fiber: the base parameter can remain a nonzero nilpotent, as E3 shows.

items.name: Perfectness of the Fourier nearby stalk
items.statement: In C2 the stalk RΨpr′(LΛ(ft′))_(x,∞′) is a perfect Λ-complex for the finite, regular integral and rational coefficients used by §1.6. The finite-level constructibility/Tor bounds must be proved uniformly to pass to the adic inverse limit; finite cohomological dimension of lim alone is not a substitute for the full comparison.

items.name: Integral and finite coefficient reduction of the trace
items.statement: For A=Zℓ[ζp] and the perfect compatible nearby complexes of A22, scalar extension to Qℓ(ζp) and reduction modulo ℓ^n commute with the trace, and the integral trace is determined by all its reductions through A≅lim A/ℓ^n. The G-action must descend through the same comparisons.

items.name: Connected curve cover with an extended coefficient endomorphism
items.statement: For each fixed n>0 and σ≠1 in the spread-out setup, apply A17 to the Fourier kernel over A¹t′, obtaining a connected integral finite surjective cover P′→P¹t′, a ULA extension L and α extending σ. Justify the finite curve cover from the alteration by normalization; no simultaneous lifted G-action is inferred.

uses.how: Relative trace is constant on the connected parameter cover
The infinity fiber identifies with nearby cycles

items.name: Relative trace is constant on the connected parameter cover
items.statement: In A24, (X^σ)red={x}. Nil-invariance of étale duality identifies H⁰(X^σ×P′,K/P′) with H⁰(P′,Λ)=Λ, and restriction to the chosen points over 0′ and ∞′ is an isomorphism. Hence both restrictions of the relative trace coincide.

items.name: Trace of the constant sheaf is fixed intersection length
items.statement: For the smooth finite-type k-scheme in A20 with isolated fixed locus, the ordinary Lefschetz–Verdier trace of (Λ,σ) is (ΔX·Γσ)X×X=length(OXσ)=−aX,G(σ). The local intersection equality needs the isolated complete-intersection calculation, not just set-theoretic fixed points.
items.locator: Theorem 1.6 p.615; SGA5 III Ex.4.3; Fulton Prop.7.1(b)

items.name: The infinity fiber identifies with nearby cycles
items.statement: Under A24 the ULA extension restricts at ∞′ to the nearby cycles of the original kernel, using goodness on the one-dimensional base and the canonical σ-action. This is a coefficient/action-compatible isomorphism, not equality with the original zero-extension stalk.

items.name: Trace of a point-supported complex
items.statement: For a perfect coefficient complex P on x and closed immersion i:x→X, proper-pushforward compatibility identifies the relative fixed-locus trace of i*P with the ordinary alternating trace of its endomorphism on P. Apply this only after the support theorem F18, whose proof is independent of A29.

items.name: Equivariant Fourier nearby-cycle trace formula
items.statement: Under all of C2, for σ∈G with σ≠1, −aX,G(σ)=Tr(σ;RΨpr′(L(ft′))_(x,∞′)) in Qℓ(ζp). Compare the two restrictions in A25, identify the zero fiber by A26 and the infinity fiber by A27/A28, and pass through finite coefficients by A23. No assertion at σ=1 is made here.

items.name: Perfect-complex and representation Grothendieck groups
items.statement: For a ring A let K•(A)=K0(Dperf(A)). For finite G and L of characteristic zero define RL(G)=K•(L[G]). Reuse the existing TriangulatedK0 carrier, constructing the perfect subcategory and its ring product under the appropriate tensor conventions.
items.note: Only the perfect coefficient-category instance and comparison with existing K0 are new here. Import bounded projective-complex construction from K.4:construction and the ordinary derived enhancement; do not construct another higher K-theory spectrum.

uses.how: Perfect representation K0 equals the split representation ring
Derived tensor pairing on the relevant K0 groups

items.name: Perfect representation K0 equals the split representation ring
items.statement: For finite G and characteristic-zero L, Maschke semisimplicity identifies RL(G) with the existing repRing L G via the alternating sum of cohomology representations. Prove compatibility with tensor and character maps. This comparison is missing even though both generic carriers are built.

items.name: Projective integral Swan module
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension of K as in C3 with group Δ, choose a finitely generated projective Zℓ[Δ]-module SwΔ realizing the Swan character. Include the appropriate self-duality/right-module convention used for tensor-Hom comparison. This is stronger than numerical conductor integrality.

uses.how: Compatible tower trivializing finite reductions
Exactness of the fixed-tower torsion Swan functor
Full regular Fourier class is total dimension, with a minus sign
Katz canonical-extension Swan model

items.name: Compatible tower trivializing finite reductions
items.statement: A tower K=K0⊂K1⊂… of finite Galois extensions, Δi=Gal(Ki/K), trivializes M when every derived reduction M⊗ᴸZℓ Z/ℓ^n has action factoring through some Δi. Choose isomorphisms SwΔi+1⊗Zℓ[Δi+1]Zℓ[Δi]≅SwΔi once and use them coherently along the chain.

uses.how: Existence of a trivializing tower
Torsion Swan and total-dimension modules

items.name: Existence of a trivializing tower
items.statement: For a finitely generated module over the finite/integral ℓ-adic coefficient rings of §2.2 with continuous Γ-action, choose finite Galois quotients trivializing all finite derived reductions and take successive composita to obtain B04.

items.name: Torsion Swan and total-dimension modules
items.statement: For torsion Λ, a continuous finite Λ-module M trivialized by the chosen tower, set swΛ(M)=SwΔi⊗Zℓ[Δi]M for large i, identified using the chosen transitions, and dtΛ(M)=swΛ(M)⊕M. A commuting G-action descends to both modules. Only this G-action is required downstream; specify any retained Γ-action separately.

uses.how: Exactness of the fixed-tower torsion Swan functor
Integral inverse-limit Swan module
Finite coefficient local total-dimension identity

items.name: Exactness of the fixed-tower torsion Swan functor
items.statement: On the fixed-tower category of B06, swΛ is exact because the Swan module is projective over Zℓ[Δi]. Equivalently use its correct self-dual Hom presentation. Commuting G-actions and finite coefficient changes are respected.

items.name: Integral inverse-limit Swan module
items.statement: For Λ finite projective over Zℓ and M finite over Λ with continuous Γ×G action trivialized by B04, define swΛ(M)=limn swΛ/ℓ^n(M⊗Z/ℓ^n); dtΛ(M)=swΛ(M)⊕M. Construct the transition system using the fixed tower data before taking the limit.

uses.how: Exactness of the integral Swan construction
Tower independence after rationalization

items.name: Exactness of the integral Swan construction
items.statement: For a short exact sequence of finite Λ-modules with continuous Γ×G-actions trivialized by one chosen compatible Swan tower, the integral functor swΛ of B08 is exact. The proof uses finite-fibre inverse limits and the boundedly vanishing reduction kernels B19. Projective Swan-module existence remains a separate input.

items.name: Tower independence after rationalization
items.statement: For a fixed Γ×G-stable OL-lattice N, the class swOL(N)⊗Q in RL(G) is independent of the trivializing tower and chosen transition isomorphisms. Compare finite-level traces using a common finite Galois extension, pass to the complete coefficient ring and use characteristic injectivity. This does not assert a canonical integral isomorphism.

items.name: Lattice independence after rationalization
items.statement: For two stable OL-lattices N,N′ in M, replace by N+N′ and compare an inclusion with torsion quotient. By exactness B09, the rationalized Swan classes agree since the Swan construction of the quotient remains torsion.

items.name: Rational Swan and total-dimension classes
items.statement: For M finite-dimensional over L with continuous Γ×G action, define sw(M)∈RL(G) as the common rational class from B10–B11 and dt(M)=sw(M)+[M]. Extend additively to bounded complexes with the relevant finite-dimensional cohomology and continuous actions.

uses.how: Rational equivariant local total-dimension identity

items.name: Equivariant perfect trace
items.statement: For a commutative Noetherian Λ and finite G let DΛ-perf(Λ[G]) be the full subcategory of complexes whose underlying Λ-complex is perfect. For σ∈G, left multiplication on the right regular Λ[G]-module induces ϕσ on its tensor with F; define Tr(σ;F) as the perfect Λ-trace of ϕσ.

uses.how: Integral and finite coefficient reduction of the trace
Trace of a point-supported complex
Strictification for equivariant perfect complexes and maps
Derived tensor pairing on the relevant K0 groups

items.name: Strictification for equivariant perfect complexes and maps
items.statement: For a triangle M′→M→M″ in DΛ-perf(Λ[G]), find bounded complexes of finitely generated Λ[G]-modules projective over Λ representing M′ and M, with an actual chain map representing the given derived morphism. Compare M″ with its mapping cone. The finite-resolution/truncation construction must be supplied, not assumed from Λ[G]-perfectness.

items.name: Additivity of the group-element trace
items.statement: For σ∈G and an exact triangle in DΛ-perf(Λ[G]), Tr(σ;M)=Tr(σ;M′)+Tr(σ;M″). This yields K0(DΛ-perf(Λ[G]))→Λ. The proof uses B14 and chain-level cone additivity; it is not an assertion of additivity for arbitrary endomorphism triples in an abstract triangulated category.

items.name: Finite-coefficient trace detects rational class equality
items.statement: For the perfect compatible integral models used in §2.5, equality of all finite-level group-element traces gives equality of integral traces and then, over characteristic-zero L, equality in RL(G) by B02 and L04. Coefficient completeness, perfectness and G-compatibility are hypotheses.

items.name: Local Fourier transform from 0 to infinity
items.statement: For the strict henselian traits at 0 and ∞′ in equal characteristic p, and a finite-dimensional ℓ-adic local system V on the punctured first trait, define the local Fourier transform as the degree-one vanishing/nearby-cycle stalk of Lψ(tt′)⊗V! at (0,∞′). Relate the RΦ and RΨ descriptions using zero extension in the second coordinate.

uses.how: Local Fourier concentration
Laumon's Artin representation from the augmentation ideal
Fourier family relating Katz and Laumon models
Exactness of the local Fourier functor
Local Fourier rank formula
Local Fourier preservation of Swan conductor

items.name: Local Fourier concentration
items.statement: In F01 the local vanishing-cycle complex is supported at the closed pair and concentrated in cohomological degree 1.

items.name: Laumon's Artin representation from the augmentation ideal
items.statement: For a finite Galois cover of strictly henselian equal-characteristic traits with algebraically closed residue field and group H, apply F(0,∞′) to ker(Qbarℓ[H]→Qbarℓ), using the commuting left and right H-actions. The remaining right H-action defines ArtH.

uses.how: Character and coefficient field of Laumon's realization

items.name: Character and coefficient field of Laumon's realization
items.statement: Under F03, the right H-character of ArtH is the classical Artin character, and the construction is defined over Qℓ(ψ(1)). This alone is not the Qℓ-rationality proof for the higher-dimensional Artin character.

items.name: Regular Galois local-system descent
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension ξ→η with group Δ and a finite coefficient ring Λ with p invertible, let D=f*Λξ as a right Λ[Δ]-local system. For a complex M with commuting left Δ and G actions construct its associated η-local system M̃ and the isomorphism D!⊗ᴸΛ[Δ]M≅M̃! on S.

uses.how: Perfect regular Fourier complex over the group ring
Equivariant nearby-cycle tensor interchange

items.name: Perfect regular Fourier complex over the group ring
items.statement: For D as in F05, the stalk N=RΨq′(LΛ(tt′)⊗ᴸΛ D!)_(0,∞′) is perfect as a right Λ[Δ]-complex, not merely as a Λ-complex. Supply the group-ring constructible finite-Tor argument and finite cohomological bound.

items.name: Full regular Fourier class is total dimension, with a minus sign
items.statement: For the finite coefficient setup of F06, in K0(Dperf(Λ[Δ]op)) one has −[N]=[(SwΔ⊕Zℓ[Δ])⊗ZℓΛ]. The augmentation-ideal Fourier realization gives Artin, whereas the full regular input gives Artin plus the trivial representation, equivalently Swan plus regular. The integral projective-class comparison needs separate verification beyond the rational character calculation.

items.name: Derived tensor pairing on the relevant K0 groups
items.statement: For finite Δ,G, N,N′ perfect right Λ[Δ]-complexes and M∈DΛ-perf(Λ[Δ×G]), [N]=[N′] implies [N⊗ᴸΛ[Δ]M]=[N′⊗ᴸΛ[Δ]M] in K0(DΛ-perf(Λ[G])). Prove preservation of the underlying Λ-perfect condition using group-ring perfectness of N; Λ-perfectness of N alone is insufficient.

items.name: Equivariant nearby-cycle tensor interchange
items.statement: For the specific finite regular local system D! and bounded coefficient context of F06, RΨq′(L⊗ᴸΛ D!⊗ᴸΛ[Δ]M)≅RΨq′(L⊗ᴸΛ D!)⊗ᴸΛ[Δ]M. Use a bounded Ψ⁰-acyclic model on the sheaf side and a possibly unbounded finite-free group-module resolution; justify totalization and acyclicity by the stated finite cohomological dimension.

items.name: Finite coefficient local total-dimension identity
items.statement: For finite Λ with p invertible and M a finite Λ-free module carrying Δ×G action as in F05, the fixed-quotient total-dimension class is −[RΨq′(LΛ(tt′)⊗M̃!)_(0,∞′)] in K0(DΛ-perf(Λ[G])). Apply F07 through F08 and F09; this proof does not use Theorem 1.6.

items.name: Rational equivariant local total-dimension identity
items.statement: For M finite-dimensional over Qℓ(ζp) with continuous Γ×G action, dt(M)=−[RΨq′(L(tt′)⊗M̃!)_(0,∞′)] in RQℓ(ζp)(G). Descend to a stable lattice and finite coefficients, then use B16. Retain all character values, including σ=1, for this class equality.

items.name: Katz–Laumon vanishing for the constant full-trait input
items.statement: For the strict traits and nontrivial ψ in F01, the nearby-cycle stalk at (0,∞′) of L(tt′) tensored with the constant sheaf on the full first trait vanishes. This is distinct from the nonzero rank-one local Fourier transform of the punctured-trait constant sheaf extended by zero.
items.locator: §2.5 support proof p.620; Katz–Laumon vanishing input

items.name: Localization converts the local identity to vanishing cycles
items.statement: For a bounded constructible Λ[G]-coefficient complex F on S in the admissible rational setting, localization together with F11 and F12 gives dt(RΦid(F))=−[RΨq′(L(tt′)⊗q*F)_(0,∞′)]. Extend from sheaves to bounded complexes by exactness and K0 additivity, stating the finite-dimensionality assumptions.

items.name: Projection formula on the strict-local Milnor-fiber diagram
items.statement: In C2, for a geometric y of the special fiber form g:(X×S′)_(y,∞′)→(S×S′)_(0,∞′). Because L(tt′) is lisse on the generic second-coordinate fiber, the required Rg*-projection formula holds there. This is the specific source-qualified comparison, not a claim that Rg* satisfies every projection formula without hypotheses.

items.name: Milnor-fiber base change to the one-dimensional parameter
items.statement: For f(y):X(y)→S in C2, the goodness comparison identifies Rg*Λ over the generic second-coordinate fiber with the pullback of Rf(y)*Λ. Combine with F14 and the stalk formula to identify the y-stalk of the Fourier nearby cycles with the transform of Rf(y)*Λ.

items.name: Smooth local fiber has constant pushforward
items.statement: In C2, for y≠x the local acyclicity of the smooth map implies Rf(y)*Λ≅Λ in the strict-local comparison of §2.5. This is used only in that stalk setting, not as a global equality Rf*Λ=Λ for every smooth morphism.

items.name: Vanishing cycles commute with the strict-local pushforward comparison
items.statement: For the coefficient objects in §2.5, RΦid(Rf(y)*F)≅(RΦf F)y with the same G-action when y is fixed. Prove this from the corresponding specialization triangles and Milnor-fiber stalk comparison.

items.name: Fourier nearby cycles are supported at the isolated point
items.statement: Under C2, RΨpr′(L(ft′)) on X×{∞′} has support contained in {(x,∞′)}. For y≠x use F15, F16 and F12. This proof is independent of the trace formula A29, so importing it in A28 creates no cycle.

items.name: Vanishing-cycle total-dimension class equals negative Fourier class
items.statement: Under C2, dt((RΦfΛ)x)=−[RΨpr′(L(ft′))_(x,∞′)] in RQℓ(ζp)(G). Combine F13, F15 and F17. No sign is absorbed into the definition of dt or the unshifted nearby-cycle functor.

items.name: Kato–Saito–Saito reduction to the geometric nonidentity trace formula
items.statement: Abe §2.6 invokes Kato–Saito–Saito Lemma 5.3 to reduce both assertions of the regular-local Serre conjecture to their Conjecture 5.1 over k{t}, k algebraically closed of characteristic p. A29 and F19 give Tr(σ;dt((RΦfΛ)x))=aX,G(σ) for σ≠1 in that geometry. The reduction from arbitrary C1 rings, the regular-character correction, actual positivity and Qℓ descent must be transcribed from the unread external lemma before this item is closed.

items.name: Katz canonical-extension Swan model
items.statement: For the finite Galois extension in §3.1, choose a lisse extension of the regular local system on Gm agreeing near 0 and tame at ∞. With j:Gm→A¹ and j′:A¹→P¹, form H¹(P¹,j′!Rj*Reg~); Katz's theorem identifies this G-module with the Swan representation. Canonical extension and the concentration proof are external supplier gates.

uses.how: Fourier family relating Katz and Laumon models

items.name: Fourier family relating Katz and Laumon models
items.statement: Let M=j′!Rj*Reg~⊗L(tt′) on P¹t×P¹t′ and C=Rpr′*M with no global shift. Compare its 0′ stalk to RΓ(P¹,M0′), and its generic/special nearby cycles to the local Fourier model. Retain the derived degrees explicitly.

uses.how: Corrected virtual comparison of the two Swan/Artin models

items.name: Corrected virtual comparison of the two Swan/Artin models
items.statement: With the concentration and comparison hypotheses of R01–R02 proved, the unshifted nearby-cycle class is −([SwG]+[Λ[G]]). Equivalently, its negative is total dimension. The printed positive formula in §3.1 omits the degree-one sign, as E2 records; the main Proposition 2.5 already has the correct negative sign.

items.name: Identity trace and curve Milnor number
items.statement: In dimension one, the identity Fourier trace is −μ_f, with μ_f the different exponent in the smooth-curve setting. In dimension n the corrected formula is (−1)^n μ_f, as R05; the former unresolved sign convention is now explicit. The transitive characteristic-cycle/Fulton suppliers remain G-REMARKS.

items.name: Exactness of the local Fourier functor
items.statement: In F01's ℓ-adic equal-characteristic trait setting, F(0,∞′) is an exact functor on the category of continuous finite-dimensional local representations.

items.name: Local Fourier rank formula
items.statement: For V in F01, rank(F(0,∞′)(V))=rank(V)+Swan(V). In particular the unramified rank-one input has a one-dimensional degree-one transform.

items.name: Local Fourier preservation of Swan conductor
items.statement: For V in F01, Swan(F(0,∞′)(V))=Swan(V); the output has slopes strictly less than one. The slope-filtration infrastructure is an external input, not assumed implemented here.

items.name: Relative Verdier dual represents the categorical dual
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of A07, the dual object of (X,F) is (X,DX/S F). Evaluation and coevaluation are the diagonal correspondences with the usual evaluation and the image of idF under the duality comparison.

items.name: Bounded-complex Euler–Poincaré identity in abelian K0
items.statement: For an essentially small abelian category and a cochain complex strictly supported in [a,b], its alternating term class in AbelianK0 over any finite set containing [a,b] equals its alternating cohomology class. A quasi-isomorphism between two such bounded complexes preserves the Euler class over a finite set containing both supports.

items.name: Bounded categorical K0 comparisons
items.statement: Import the upstream Layer 2 comparison of split K0 with the bounded homotopy category and the abelian bounded-derived comparison with alternating homology. These are planned, not fully built by the pinned Euler–Poincaré identity; the finite-group perfect-category and character compatibility is B02.

items.name: Bounded projective-complex coefficient model
items.statement: Import the bounded finitely generated projective complexes with quasi-isomorphisms and degreewise split cofibrations from GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.4:construction. Only this early coefficient model is needed here, not its later S-construction spectrum or delooping theorem.

uses.how: Perfect-complex and representation Grothendieck groups

items.name: Compatible choices in finite inverse systems
items.statement: For a directed preorder J and a functor F:Jᵒᵖ→Type with every F(j) finite and nonempty, the set of compatible sections is nonempty. No surjectivity assumption on transition maps is needed.

items.name: Projective modules lift maps through surjections
items.statement: Over any semiring R, a projective left R-module P has the lifting property for a surjective linear map M→N and any linear map P→N. Use the opposite ring for right modules.

items.name: Flat tensor preserves exact sequences over a commutative ring
items.statement: Let R be commutative and M flat over R. Tensoring an exact pair N→N′→N″ with M on either side preserves exactness. This library import is used for the commutative henselian comparison, not directly over a noncommutative group ring.

items.name: Finite Swan modules commute with coefficient reduction
items.statement: Fix the compatible Swan tower of B04 and a finite Λ-module M. For S_n(M)=sw(M/ℓ^nM), there are compatible isomorphisms S_(n+1)(M)/ℓ^n S_(n+1)(M)≅S_n(M). Every S_n is a finite set, and the transition maps are surjective.

items.name: Effectivity and finite generation of the Swan inverse system
items.statement: For the S_n(M) of B17, S(M)=lim S_n(M) is finite over Λ, is ℓ-adically complete, and S(M)/ℓ^n S(M)≅S_n(M), compatibly with the commuting finite G-action.

items.name: Reduction kernels in a Swan exact sequence become zero after a bounded transition
items.statement: For 0→M′→M→M″→0 of finite Λ-modules in the fixed-tower category, set E_n=ker(M′/ℓ^nM′→M/ℓ^nM). If ℓ^c kills the Zℓ-torsion of M″, every map E_(n+c)→E_n is zero. The corresponding finite Swan-kernel transition is zero as well.

items.name: The integral Swan module of a lattice is a lattice
items.statement: Let O be the integer ring of a finite extension of Qℓ and let N be a finite free O-module in the fixed-tower category. Then sw_O(N) is finite free over O. A finite ℓ-power-torsion quotient stays ℓ-power torsion under sw.

items.name: Dimension-correct identity trace of the Fourier nearby stalk
items.statement: For a smooth n-dimensional X over a perfect field of characteristic p, constant coefficients of characteristic different from p, and f to a smooth curve with an isolated critical point x, write μ_f=(zero-section,df)_x. Under the Fourier comparison F19, the identity trace on the Fourier nearby stalk equals (−1)^n μ_f. In particular it is −μ_f for curves and +μ_f for surfaces.

items.name: A nodal surface tests the Milnor sign
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed of odd characteristic p, let X be the base change of A²_(u,v)→A¹_t, t=uv, to the strict henselization at t=0, and let C2 act by (u,v)↦(−u,−v). Then X is regular and flat over the trait, f is smooth off the origin, and the nonidentity fixed scheme is the reduced origin. The Milnor intersection length is1, so the identity Fourier trace is +1, whereas the dimension-free −μ_f formula gives −1.

uses.how: Counterchecks the necessity of the dimension sign and E6.
